estimand.description: Age coefficient in the working arithmetic-scale regression TG ~ age + sex + BMI among eligible adults aged 40-79; this map does not define a survey-weighted estimator.

estimand.population: US noninstitutionalized adults aged 40-79 satisfying this task eligibility; no target outcomes available to the builder.
estimand.measurement: Fasting serum TG in mg/dL, task legacy_proxy glycerol-blanked measurement context; exact source equivalence is an assumption.
estimand.selection: Task eligible complete observed age/sex/BMI rows, morning examination and 8.5 to <24 hours fasting; no outcome-dependent subgroup boundary chosen by builder.

analyses.rationale: The requested use is unchanged. Exact Tromso joint cells now supply a numerical surface replacing the inherited legacy mean log cross-ratio, with original reference-age/reference-BMI positive curves retained. This resolves the missing-table gap and permits age-dependent nonlinear BMI behavior; it does not identify the requested target functional. Full transfer, interpolation, global reference-curve continuation and legacy-scale estimand mapping are assumptions; no source/target output has been used for tuning.

gaps.description: Published adjusted joint log ratios are neither the requested working age coefficient, curvature functional nor raw arithmetic subgroup means.
gaps.consequence: The chosen interaction departure addresses only one structural component; target analytical results are unvalidated.

gaps.description: Korean families, initially healthy US women, Norwegian adults40+ and Chinese longitudinal cohorts differ from the task population of US adults40-79.
gaps.consequence: Population transport and age restriction are assumptions.

gaps.description: Nonfasting Tromso serum, fasting source plasma, assay/glycerol handling and target fasting context differ.
gaps.consequence: Time-since-meal adjustment does not establish fasting or assay equivalence.

gaps.description: Tromso excludes TG>10mmol/L and had65%attendance; medication/health/family selections differ among the other sources.
gaps.consequence: Selection can change conditional relationships and residual tails.

gaps.description: The exact joint table resolves prior missing ratios but reports category contrasts conditional on extra covariates; category centers and within-bin trajectories are not measured.
gaps.consequence: Bilinear interpolation and integrating unmeasured covariates remain assumptions.

gaps.description: Source models include extra lifestyle/metabolic covariates. Male Tromso education/drug adjustment remains inconsistent across supplement rows, footnote and figure descriptions.
gaps.consequence: Source adjusted effects need not equal a reduced age/sex/BMI model.

gaps.description: Tromso ratios concern exponentiated log-TG predictions. China-PAR per-SD mixed-effects scaling remains unresolved. Oh strata have arithmetic/geometric ambiguity.
gaps.consequence: Constant within-sex residual log variance is an explicit legacy-scale model bridge, not established source evidence; the affine unblanked assay map breaks ratio equality.

gaps.description: The inherited legacy log cross-ratio is replaced with D; reference-age and reference-BMI positive mean curves and residual CV remain inherited. Their global continuation is assumed.
gaps.consequence: The total legacy mean cross-ratio is exp(D), but total source joint ratios are not reproduced because main-effect curves differ. Complete source/target laws remain unidentified.

gaps.description: All28 Tromso CIs are retained, but shared-reference covariance, transport and interpolation uncertainty are unavailable. Sample-count and exact CI anomalies are retained.
gaps.consequence: No posterior surface, contrast CI or inferential calibration is claimed; replay seeds measure only Monte Carlo variation.
